result_text: # Track 15 — SHAP Integration for Image Classifiers (FR-005) **Stream D (Explainability) · Feeds `explainability.py` · Research only, no repo edits** ## 0. Cross-track flags (read first) - **Schema:** proposes a new `ExplanationResult` output shape (§2). This is **not** added to `schema.py` — locked M1 schema (`SubjectRecord`, `MetricResult`) is unchanged. Needs schema-owner sign-off before any real field is added. - **Strategy pattern:** proposes an `ExplainerBackend` ABC parallel to `FairnessBackend`. `fairness/base.py`'s actual ABC conventions belong to **Track 17** — this design should be reconciled with Track 17's pattern, not implemented independently. - **"Flagged disparity" trigger:** which `MetricResult` rows count as "flagged" (p-value/CI/DIR thresholds) is fairness-engine/report-generation logic (Tracks 09–14, 17, and report tracks 05–08), not decided here. §2 assumes a boolean `is_flagged` predicate exists upstream and consumes it. - **Proxy detection:** §4 covers only the SHAP-side mechanic the track prompt asked for (aggregate/differenced attribution maps). Deeper proxy-detection methodology is **Track 16**'s dedicated scope (Phase 3) — §4 is a primitive Track 16 can build on, not a substitute for it. - **New dependency risk:** semantic region labeling (eyes/nose/skin-swatch) for proxy interpretation requires a face-landmark detector (e.g. dlib/mediapipe) not currently in the tech stack (`CONTEXT.md` §Tech Stack). Flagged as a dependency decision for the team, not resolved here. --- ## 1. SHAP variant selection | Explainer | Type | Works on ResNet-34/224×224? | Speed | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | **KernelExplainer** | Model-agnostic, LIME-style weighted linear regression over coalitions | Technically yes, practically no | Exponential in # features → intractable on raw pixels without manual superpixel reduction | Excluded — superseded by PartitionExplainer for images | | **PartitionExplainer** (via `shap.Explainer(f, masker)`) | Model-agnostic, black-box, hierarchical (Owen-value) coalition structure over image regions | Yes — only needs `f(images) -> probs`, no architecture access | Quadratic, not exponential, in region count | **Recommended default.** Works with any model exposed as a callable (PyTorch, ONNX, a remote inference endpoint) — matches `ModelInterface`'s dual-mode contract (in-process object OR predictions file) better than gradient-based methods, which need direct tensor/autograd access | | **GradientExplainer** (expected gradients / SmoothGrad+IntegratedGradients hybrid) | PyTorch-native, needs the actual `nn.Module` and autograd | Yes, well-suited to CNNs | Fast (few dozen background samples, single/few backward passes) | Best for `InProcessInterface` once WP2 wires in real model weights; **cannot** be used against `PredictionsFileInterface`-only audits (no model object, no gradients) | | **DeepExplainer** (DeepLIFT-based) | PyTorch-native | Yes, historically the fastest | Fast, similar to GradientExplainer | Deprioritized: known hook-compatibility issues with in-place ReLU / BatchNorm patterns in modern `torchvision.models.resnet34`; SHAP's own docs steer new PyTorch image work toward GradientExplainer/PartitionExplainer over DeepExplainer | **Decision:** default to **PartitionExplainer** (`shap.maskers.Image` + `shap.Explainer`), because it works identically whether the audited model came in via `InProcessInterface` or `PredictionsFileInterface` re-wrapped as a scoring function — the same reason the project already favors black-box-friendly design (`PredictionsFileInterface` is the non-negotiable core per the cut-list). Offer **GradientExplainer** as an opt-in fast path when `InProcessInterface` + a real PyTorch object is available (WP2-dependent). ### Runtime estimates (engineering estimates — NOT benchmarked; flag for empirical validation, e.g. as a Track 18-adjacent task) | Explainer | 1 image | 100 images | 1,000 images | |---|---|---|---| | PartitionExplainer, CPU, `max_evals≈300` | ~10–30s | ~15–50 min | ~2.5–8 hr | | PartitionExplainer, GPU (batched `max_evals`) | ~1–3s | ~2–5 min | ~20–50 min | | GradientExplainer, GPU, ~50 background samples | ~0.2–0.5s | ~20–50s | ~3–8 min | | GradientExplainer, CPU | ~1–3s | ~2–5 min | ~20–50 min | **Design implication:** because FR-005 says "every flagged disparity," not "every image," realistic volume is bounded by the number of flagged `MetricResult` rows × a bounded sample per subgroup (§2), not by the full 108,501-image FairFace corpus. That keeps even the slow CPU/PartitionExplainer path tractable — full-corpus SHAP is out of scope and should stay that way. --- ## 2. Integration with BiasAperture ### 2.1 Trigger point SHAP explanation is a **post-processing step on the detection engine's output**, not part of ingestion or metric computation: ``` ModelInterface.get_predictions() → SubjectRecord stream │ ▼ FairnessBackend(s) → MetricResult rows (Tracks 09–14, 17 — untouched by this track) │ ▼ filter: is_flagged(MetricResult) ← threshold logic owned upstream ▼ ExplainerBackend.explain_subgroup(subgroup, SubjectRecord sample, model) │ ▼ ExplanationResult rows → report/generator.py (Tracks 05–08) ``` ### 2.2 Proposed interface (draft — not a schema.py edit) ```python class ExplainerBackend(ABC): """Mirrors FairnessBackend's Strategy pattern (see Track 17 for the canonical ABC conventions — this shape is a proposal to reconcile, not an independent implementation).""" @abstractmethod def explain( self, records: Iterable[SubjectRecord], # locked schema, unchanged model: Any, # ModelInterface-compatible task_head: str, # which audited-task output to attribute ) -> Iterator["ExplanationResult"]: raise NotImplementedError @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class ExplanationResult: # PROPOSED — needs schema-owner sign-off image_id: str # ties back to SubjectRecord.image_id subgroup: str # same composite-key format as MetricResult.subgroup task_head: str # "race" | "gender" | "age" | audit-specific predicted_class: str shap_values: "np.ndarray" # (H, W, 3) — not report-serializable directly base_value: float explainer_backend: Literal["partition", "gradient"] png_path: str # rendered artifact for report embedding (§3) ``` ### 2.3 Sampling strategy (needed — flag for team decision) A flagged subgroup can have hundreds/thousands of members; SHAP should not run on all of them. Proposal: seeded random sample, `k = min(n_subgroup, 20)`, same `random_state` convention as the bootstrap CI code (Track 11) so runs are reproducible. **This constant is not yet locked anywhere — flag for whoever owns `fairness/statistics.py` to keep the seeding convention consistent project-wide.** --- ## 3. Visualization ### 3.1 `shap.plots.image` (the current API; `shap.image_plot` is the legacy alias) ```python shap.plots.image(shap_values, show=False) ``` Output: a matplotlib figure — one row per input image, one column per explained output class, each cell a red/blue-overlaid heatmap on the original image (red = pixels pushing toward that class, blue = pixels pushing away). This is the standard visualization for both PartitionExplainer and GradientExplainer output, since both return `(H, W, 3)`-shaped attributions per class. ### 3.2 Saving for report embedding ```python buf = BytesIO() fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight") b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii") ``` Then in the Jinja2 template: ```html ``` **PNG over SVG:** matplotlib *can* emit SVG (`format="svg"`), but the heatmap layer is a rasterized `imshow` regardless of container format — SVG buys vector-crispness only for axis labels/text, not the attribution map itself. Recommend **PNG only**, consistent with how force plots are already embedded elsewhere in similar SHAP+Jinja2 workflows, to avoid a second image pipeline for marginal benefit. ### 3.3 Report layout recommendation For each flagged subgroup pair (e.g. `race=Black` vs. `race=White` on the same metric), show side-by-side SHAP panels for a matched sample of correctly- and incorrectly-classified subjects — this is what makes the explanation *comparative* rather than a single unexplained heatmap, and is what §4 depends on. --- ## 4. Proxy variable detection (bounded to the SHAP mechanic — see §0 flag) **Aggregate/differenced attribution maps**, directly following the Kurian et al. 2024 proxy-encoding concern already cited as FR-005's justification in the lit-review matrix: 1. For a flagged subgroup pair (e.g. `race=Black` vs. `race=White`), draw the sampled sets from §2.3. 2. Compute per-image `|SHAP|` maps (magnitude, class-agnostic — "how much did any region matter") and align them (subjects are already face-aligned per the FairFace pipeline, so no additional registration step should be needed). 3. Average `|SHAP|` maps within each subgroup → two mean heatmaps. 4. Subtract: `diff = mean_map_A - mean_map_B`. Concentration of `diff` in low-frequency skin-region areas (broad cheek/forehead zones) versus structural regions (eyes/nose/mouth edges) is the *visual* signal Kurian et al.'s methodology looks for — texture/lighting-style proxy encoding shows up as diffuse regional weight, not edge-aligned weight. **What this section deliberately does NOT do** (Track 16's job): define a statistical test for "is this proxy encoding," attach semantic region labels (needs a landmark detector — new dependency, flagged in §0), or make any causal claim. It only produces the two aggregate maps and the difference map as inputs Track 16's methodology can consume. --- ## 5. Complete Python code example ```python """ Reference prototype only — not a repo edit. For WP4 owner review. Loads dchen236/FairFace's ResNet-34 (race_7, 18-way fc head: race[0:7], gender[7:9], age[9:18] — per predict.py's known output layout), runs PartitionExplainer SHAP on one image, saves a report-embeddable PNG. """ from __future__ import annotations import base64 from dataclasses import dataclass from io import BytesIO from pathlib import Path from typing import Literal import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import shap import torch import torch.nn as nn from PIL import Image from torchvision import models, transforms _HEAD_SLICES = {"race": slice(0, 7), "gender": slice(7, 9), "age": slice(9, 18)} _PREPROCESS = transforms.Compose([ transforms.Resize((224, 224)), transforms.ToTensor(), transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225]), ]) def load_fairface_resnet34(checkpoint_path: str | Path, device: str = "cpu") -> nn.Module: """dchen236/FairFace race_7 checkpoint: ResNet-34 with an 18-way fc head.""" model = models.resnet34(weights=None) model.fc = nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, 18) state_dict = torch.load(checkpoint_path, map_location=device) model.load_state_dict(state_dict) model.to(device).eval() return model def make_prediction_fn(model: nn.Module, head: Literal["race", "gender", "age"], device: str): """f(X: uint8 ndarray[N,H,W,3]) -> softmax probs[N, n_classes] — the black-box shape shap.Explainer expects; works for any task_head.""" idx = _HEAD_SLICES[head] def f(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: batch = torch.stack( [_PREPROCESS(Image.fromarray(img.astype(np.uint8))) for img in x] ).to(device) with torch.no_grad(): probs = torch.softmax(model(batch)[:, idx], dim=1) return probs.cpu().numpy() return f @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class ExplanationResult: # proposed shape, see §2.2 image_id: str task_head: str shap_values: np.ndarray base_value: float explainer_backend: str def explain_one_image( image_path: str | Path, model: nn.Module, head: Literal["race", "gender", "age"], device: str = "cpu", max_evals: int = 300, ) -> tuple["shap.Explanation", np.ndarray]: img = np.array(Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB").resize((224, 224))) x = img[np.newaxis, ...] f = make_prediction_fn(model, head, device) masker = shap.maskers.Image("inpaint_telea", x[0].shape) explainer = shap.Explainer(f, masker) # dispatches to PartitionExplainer shap_values = explainer( x, max_evals=max_evals, batch_size=32, outputs=shap.Explanation.argsort.flip[:2], # top-2 predicted classes ) return shap_values, img def save_shap_visualization(shap_values: "shap.Explanation", out_path: str | Path) -> str: """Render shap.plots.image, save PNG to disk, return base64 for Jinja2.""" shap.plots.image(shap_values, show=False) fig = plt.gcf() fig.savefig(out_path, format="png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight") buf = BytesIO() fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight") plt.close(fig) return base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii") if __name__ == "__main__": model = load_fairface_resnet34("res34_fair_align_multi_7_20190809.pt") shap_values, img = explain_one_image( "sample_face_aligned.jpg", model, head="gender", max_evals=300, ) b64 = save_shap_visualization(shap_values, "shap_gender_explanation.png") print(f"saved shap_gender_explanation.png — {len(b64)} b64 chars for report embed") ``` *(Optional fast path, PyTorch-native, for `InProcessInterface` only:)* ```python background = torch.stack([_PREPROCESS(Image.open(p)) for p in sample_paths[:50]]) explainer = shap.GradientExplainer(model, background) shap_values = explainer.shap_values(_PREPROCESS(Image.open(image_path)).unsqueeze(0)) ``` --- ## 6. Open items for the team 1. Sign off on `ExplanationResult` fields (§2.2) before anyone touches `schema.py`. 2. Reconcile `ExplainerBackend` ABC with Track 17's `FairnessBackend` conventions. 3. Decide the sampling constant/seed convention (§2.3) against Track 11's bootstrap seeding. 4. Decide whether a landmark-detector dependency is acceptable for Track 16's proxy-region labeling (§4) — not decided here. 5. Empirically benchmark §1's runtime table on actual project hardware before it's treated as a capacity-planning number.
